scenes.tts: Can stimulating the brain create touch in a hand a person cannot feel? And does it help?
scenes.visual: Title card: Writing Touch. A hand map drawn over somatosensory cortex, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Can stimulating the brain create touch in a hand a person cannot feel? And does it help?

scenes.tts: In one man with a spinal cord injury, electrodes in sensory cortex evoked sensations felt in the hand.
scenes.visual: Microelectrode arrays in somatosensory cortex; a sensation lights on the hand. Label: Flesher and colleagues, 2016.
scenes.narration: In one man with a spinal cord injury, electrodes in sensory cortex evoked sensations felt in the hand.

scenes.tts: A responsive electrode evokes touch in a region of the hand, its projected field. Fields can overlap and change with stimulation. So each electrode is an approximate address.
scenes.visual: Electrodes light one at a time; each responsive one lights a region of the hand, and some regions overlap. Label: projected field = approximate address. An amplitude bar rises; one region grows brighter and slightly larger.
scenes.narration: A responsive electrode evokes touch in a region of the hand, its projected field. Fields can overlap and change with stimulation. So each electrode is an approximate address.

scenes.tts: Does feedback help a task? The same man moved a robotic arm, decoded from his motor cortex.
scenes.visual: A robotic arm grasping a block, driven by signals from motor cortex; touch feedback flows back to sensory cortex.
scenes.narration: Does feedback help a task? The same man moved a robotic arm, decoded from his motor cortex.

scenes.tts: With touch feedback, his median task time fell from twenty point nine seconds to ten point two.
scenes.caption: With touch feedback, his median task time fell from 20.9 seconds to 10.2.
scenes.visual: Two timers side by side: 20.9 s without feedback, 10.2 s with it. Label: Flesher and colleagues, 2021.
scenes.narration: With touch feedback, his median task time fell from 20.9 seconds to 10.2.

scenes.tts: Predict. By what percentage did his task time fall? Choose your baseline first.
scenes.visual: Blank percentage box under the timers.
scenes.narration: Predict. By what percentage did his task time fall? Choose your baseline first.

scenes.tts: About fifty-one percent, measured against the time without feedback. The working is on screen.
scenes.caption: About 51 percent, measured against the time without feedback. The working is on screen.
scenes.visual: On screen: (20.9 - 10.2) / 20.9 = 10.7 / 20.9 = 51.2 percent. Baseline 20.9 s highlighted.
scenes.narration: About 51 percent, measured against the time without feedback. The working is on screen.

scenes.tts: But these are one person's medians. They show feedback helped him, not a population effect.
scenes.visual: Label: one participant; not a population effect.
scenes.narration: But these are one person's medians. They show feedback helped him, not a population effect.

scenes.tts: Patterns across addresses can write features. In two people, several electrodes stimulated together evoked a tactile edge. Sequences evoked apparent motion.
scenes.visual: Several electrodes fire in the hand map. A line of lit regions forms an edge on the hand; then an arrow of apparent motion sweeps across it. Label: Valle and colleagues, 2025.
scenes.narration: Patterns across addresses can write features. In two people, several electrodes stimulated together evoked a tactile edge. Sequences evoked apparent motion.

scenes.tts: This is the second half of the idea. Send each group of neurons the right pattern.
scenes.visual: The one-idea box returns with a second line added: then send the right pattern.
scenes.narration: This is the second half of the idea. Send each group of neurons the right pattern.

scenes.tts: One strategy is biomimicry, copying features of the natural code. Here the scheme imitates cortical touch responses, strongest at contact onset and offset.
scenes.visual: Label: biomimicry. A plot with the axis labelled pulse amplitude over one press: the biomimetic amplitude peaks at onset and offset with a lower level between, at constant pulse spacing. Beside it, the control, whose amplitude follows indentation depth.
scenes.narration: One strategy is biomimicry, copying features of the natural code. Here the scheme imitates cortical touch responses, strongest at contact onset and offset.

scenes.tts: In three people, biomimetic stimulation felt more like a real press on some electrodes. It also needed less charge for the same felt intensity.
scenes.visual: Ratings bars per electrode, some higher for the biomimetic pattern; a smaller charge bar, labelled same perceived intensity. Label: Hobbs and colleagues, 2025.
scenes.narration: In three people, biomimetic stimulation felt more like a real press on some electrodes. It also needed less charge for the same felt intensity.

scenes.tts: That supports a strategy with evidence. It is not a law that closer copying always works better.
scenes.visual: Tag: evidence-backed strategy, not a law.
scenes.narration: That supports a strategy with evidence. It is not a law that closer copying always works better.

scenes.tts: So map where each electrode's touch is felt, and test what the person can tell apart. Then send each group a pattern it can read.
scenes.visual: End line on screen: map the fields and test what the person can tell apart; then send each group a pattern it can read.
scenes.narration: So map where each electrode's touch is felt, and test what the person can tell apart. Then send each group a pattern it can read.
